answer: Convex tenure on one meadow: weight is the square of a key’s consecutive judged epochs on its ridge, while that meadow may seal only one ridge step each epoch and locks ferrous behind every step, slashed on gaps or forks. Extra heads cannot borrow elapsed time; giving n clones one honest agent’s t-epoch weight needs n×t serialized steps from that meadow, so the bill is elapsed attested epochs plus ferrous at risk, not parallelizable or splittable.
